headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools, while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent with no isolation details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI tools and read/write application-defined files, so if ai-engineering-hub outputs are bridged into those channels, prompt injection is plausible. ai-engineering-hub has no documented isolation or parser hardening, and the pair lacks provenance controls. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into Semantic Kernel prompts, files, or MCP inputs without provenance checks, injection risk materializes.
IF Semantic Kernel treats retrieved file or tool output as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent A outputs into prompts.
Add a provenance tag to every file/tool payload before B reads it.
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only endpoints.
Review any parser that converts text into tool calls.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation guards.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel touches application context, secrets, and broad networked model providers, while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent repo with no stated data handling limits. If they share a workspace or files, B can upload contents to third-party APIs by default. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets are present, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or workspace, B can read A-produced artifacts.
IF B forwards those artifacts to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or MCP tools, contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B.
Block B from reading A output directories.
Turn off network egress for B during shared-data runs.
Store secrets outside any shared folder.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem and broad network egress; A is an agent repo with MCP/RAG focus but no explicit write surface. Even without proven overlap, B's mutable filesystem and shared-state model can conflict with A-produced artifacts if both target the same directory or memory store. Because A's write capability is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory, B can overwrite or race with A artifacts.
IF B instances share memory-store state, concurrent updates can conflict with A-generated outputs.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent.
Disable concurrent writes to shared folders.
Use file locks or a single-writer queue.
Avoid shared memory-store keys for paired runs.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG/MCP repository whose outputs may be treated as inputs. If B consumes A's text or tool results without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as authoritative context, hallucinations can propagate.
IF B triggers plugins or API calls based on A outputs without validation, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review before any action-taking step.
Insert a verification pass between A output and B tool use.
Log source provenance for every claim B consumes.
Limit B to read-only summarization of A outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while Semantic Kernel is a Microsoft SDK with broad cloud integrations and secret handling. The pair could create compliance issues if sensitive data is routed through B, but the profiles do not establish a concrete regulated-data flow. One-agent citation is sufficient because the mismatch is not explicitly pairwise documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B's cloud-connected providers, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF A is used with data subject to stricter controls than B's default integrations, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Disable cloud providers for compliance-sensitive sessions.
Review retention settings before execution.
Document the data class allowed for each agent.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
